answer: Cross-epoch behaviour fingerprinting. Each identity’s action timing skew, peer set overlap (willow) and message entropy are hashed per epoch; the next epoch must match within tolerance or the identity is gated. Attackers running many sock puppets pay continuous synchronization cost: rotating fingerprints to stay under tolerance forces fresh infrastructure, and each missed match forfeits accrued jade rewards. Divergence beyond two standard deviations triggers a reef-style isolation—new keys must self-fund a full warm-up cycle, making mass sybil upkeep exceed honest yield.
